subject: botany
question_text: Why are bryophytes called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.7, VSAQ 7. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: They live on land
lines: Bryophytes live on land, in moist and
steps.why: 'Amphibian' describes a life in two places. The plant body itself grows on land — on moist soil, rocks and tree bark — which is the land half of the comparison.
common_mistakes: Writing that bryophytes live in water. The plant grows on land; only fertilisation needs water.
steps.memory_tip: A frog lives on land but breeds in water; a bryophyte does the same, so both are called amphibians.
steps.margin_note: State the land half in one line; the reason mark is in the next step.

steps.label: Water needed for fertilisation

lines.text: They need water for sexual reproduction

lines: The antherozoids must swim through water
to reach the archegonium and the egg.
steps.why: The male gametes are flagellated and can move only through a film of water, so no fertilisation happens without water — the water half of the comparison.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 'they need water' without the reason — the swimming antherozoids are the reason.
Writing 'they need water for photosynthesis' — every plant does; the marked point is fertilisation.
steps.memory_tip: Remember the two halves as one contrast: body on land, fertilisation in water.
steps.margin_note: The boxed line plus the swimming-gamete reason completes the answer.

insider_note: The mark is for the reason — water-dependent fertilisation — not for repeating the word amphibian.
